question.text: A system consists of two types of gas molecules <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> having the same number density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>25</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The diameter of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi>A</mi></math> respectively. They suffer collisions at room temperature. The ratio of average distance covered by the molecule <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> to that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> between two successive collisions is ___________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>
